text:
Rafael Mendes: Kicking off follow-ups from today’s postmortem (Hosted API 503s deploy regression). Main gap called out: we lost ~25 min because we didn’t have deploy context in-thread + config diffs were tribal knowledge / not tenant-safe to paste.

Rafael Mendes: Action items below. Need owners + rough ETA so I can update the PM + Linear. Reply in thread w/ :raised_hand: to claim.

Rafael Mendes: 1) Incident-bot “Recent deploys” context card (service/version, rollout phase, canary status, links to PR/commit). Target: works in #incidents and #eng-oncall.
Rafael Mendes: 2) Tenant-safe config diff visibility in incident response (redaction + allowlist fields + safe rendering). Must include perms model + audit logs.
Rafael Mendes: 3) Docs/runbook updates + “first 5 min” checklist aligned w/ new cards.

Rafael Mendes: Related draft tickets: ENG-5421 (deploys card), ENG-5422 (config diff + redaction), ENG-5426 (permissioning/scopes), ENG-5431 (docs). If you already have an owner in mind, tag them.

Sean Gallagher: :eyes: Thanks Rafa. This is top of the list for SRE this month. Let’s get explicit DRI per item + date we can beta.

Miles Thornton: I can take #1 (recent deploys card) on bot side. Devon can pair on Slack rendering. I’ll coordinate w/ Release Eng for the metadata source.

Devon Price: +1. I can own the Slack block formatting + interaction (expand for more deploys, deep link). Miles owns the data hookup.

Rafael Mendes: Nice. Miles DRI, Devon support. What’s a realistic ETA to “usable in incident” (even if links only at first)?

Miles Thornton: MVP in ~1.5 weeks if deploy metadata endpoint is stable. Worst case we start by linking to DeployBot timeline + service registry.

Connor O'Brien: For deploy metadata export: Sahana + I are already working on schema in the deploy tooling. We can be DRI for the exporter side.

Sahana Iyer: Confirmed. We can get “service, image SHA, rollout phase, canary result, started_at, region” into a machine-readable feed. Linking to PR is the messy part but we can include commit SHA.

Miles Thornton: That’s enough for MVP. Bot can do “commit -> PR” best effort later.

Rafael Mendes: Great. Connor DRI for exporter. Miles DRI for bot card.

Jacob Stein: I can take #2 overall (config diff visibility) from diagnostics side, but I’ll need Platform + Security owners for the actual perms/audit.

Ethan Park: Platform can own the config diff endpoint + authz checks. Benji’s been closest to the config data model.

Benji Okafor: Yep, I’ll DRI the endpoint + diff computation. Need agreement on what fields are safe / how to render redactions.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: I’ll DRI authz scopes + break-glass flow for on-call. We need least privilege + explicit incident context-only scope.

Marcus Lin: Security can review redaction rules + do a quick threat model. But I don’t want “regex and pray” — we need an allowlist default + tests.

Kevin Osei: I’ll take audit logging: emit an audit event when bot requests config diff or privileged telemetry. Retention is already in SIEM; just need the event shape + consistent fields.

Rafael Mendes: Perfect. So #2 breakdown:
- Benji: config diff endpoint + data model
- Kaitlyn: scopes + break-glass
- Marcus: redaction review + threat model
- Kevin: audit events
- Jacob: coordinates + bot-facing integration expectations (what the card needs)

Marissa Cole: For #3 docs/runbooks, I can own the product-facing “how to use the cards” + deep link expectations. But SRE should own the actual on-call playbook edits.

Aisha Bello: I can DRI the runbook / first-5-min playbook updates (SRE side). Will need input from Miles/Jacob for “what to do if card is empty / degraded mode.”

Paula Mendes: I can track success metrics + measurement plan (context completeness score, MTTR delta during beta). Not sure if that’s #3 or separate.

Rafael Mendes: Put that as a subtask on #3, but yes we need it. Thank you.

Dylan Brooks: One more: we should explicitly state “no tenant secrets in Slack” guardrails. Suggest we add an automated test suite around redaction + a CI gate in bot repo.

Marcus Lin: +1. I want a failing test if any of the known secret-ish keys show up in Slack payload (`api_key`, `token`, `private_key`, `authorization`, etc.). Also redact long base64-ish strings.

Benji Okafor: +1 on allowlist. My proposal: endpoint returns structured diff with “field_path, old, new, classification” and the renderer decides. Anything not explicitly allowlisted => `REDACTED`.

Jacob Stein: That matches what we discussed. Also would like a “diff summary” mode: counts of changed flags, routing policy changes, quota changes, model pin changes. That’s what’s actionable in first 5 min.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: Re break-glass: we can do “Sev0/Sev1 only, on-call role, 1h TTL, must provide incident link” + audit event. But default for bot should be safe summary w/o break-glass.

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: This is the right direction. In the incident we just had, the exact changed flag name wasn’t secret, but the value / full config object could be. Summary + redacted specifics is fine.

Connor O'Brien: One nuance: config pushes can be partially rolled out. The diff needs to be anchored to “what actually served in region X at time T” not just “latest desired state.”

Ethan Park: Agree. We can version configs and query by timestamp + region. Might be phase 2 but we should at least annotate “propagation incomplete” if we detect mismatch.

Miles Thornton: For the bot UI, we can show: “Config diff (last 30m): detected changes; propagation: partial (2/5 regions)” w/ link to Console for details.

Marissa Cole: Console deep links: Chloe’s not in this thread, but we can route the links to `/console/ops/config?service=...&region=...&since=...` (placeholder). I’ll follow up with Chloe.

Rafael Mendes: Cool. Let’s pin rough dates. What can we beta in SRE rotation?

Miles Thornton: Deploy card beta: end of next week.

Benji Okafor: Config diff endpoint MVP (summary + redaction hooks): 2 weeks.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: Scopes + break-glass: 2–3 weeks depending on review cadence.

Kevin Osei: Audit events: I can do in parallel, 1 week once endpoint names are final.

Aisha Bello: Docs updates: I can have draft same week as deploy card beta.

Paula Mendes: Measurement plan: I’ll draft by EOW. Need agreement on “context completeness” definition (deploy + config + saturation present?).

Rafael Mendes: Great. I’ll update Linear:
- ENG-5421 DRI Miles (w/ Devon) + dependency Connor/Sahana
- ENG-5422 DRI Jacob coordinating, implementation DRI Benji + Marcus + Kaitlyn + Kevin
- ENG-5431 DRI Aisha, with Marissa/Paula support

Rafael Mendes: Also adding a note: “must degrade gracefully if config service/telemetry is slow; show cached + links.”

Incident Bot: Reminder: Please use :white_check_mark: when an action item is completed and include the PR/commit link.

Sean Gallagher: Thanks all. Rafa, can you schedule a 20-min checkpoint mid-next-week to ensure deploy metadata isn’t blocked? This is too important to slip.

Rafael Mendes: Will do. Sending invite.

Devon Price: Small request: when exporter is ready, can we get a staging dataset? E2E tests for #incidents need deterministic deploy events.

Sahana Iyer: Yep, we can generate a fixture feed in staging.

Jacob Stein: For redaction, let’s make sure we don’t accidentally leak tenant IDs + customer names in the diff. Even if “not secret,” we’ve been asked to minimize.

Marcus Lin: Agree. We should treat tenant identifiers as sensitive in Slack. Hash or truncate.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: +1. We can keep tenant-safe key as `tenant_ref` (internal opaque ID) and only display when channel is #incidents and user has on-call role.

Rafael Mendes: Captured. Closing this thread after I post the Linear links.

Rafael Mendes: Links:
- ENG-5421 https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-5421
- ENG-5422 https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-5422
- ENG-5426 https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-5426
- ENG-5431 https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-5431

Rafael Mendes: Thanks everyone.
